claims.explanation: OSI-027 is a dual mTORC1/mTORC2 inhibitor, so sensitivity is expected in tumors whose growth and survival depend on mTORC1/2 signaling. The strongest genomic pattern is activation of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway through PIK3CA mutation, PTEN loss, or upstream receptor/RAS/BRAF alterations, which should create oncogene addiction to mTOR and predict sensitivity in unseen lines. Conversely, intact negative feedback or alternative survival signaling may protect some lineages.

features.basis: Activating PI3K mutations drive mTORC1/2 dependence; enriched in sensitive lines.
PTEN loss hyperactivates PI3K/AKT/mTOR; seen in sensitive breast, melanoma, and endometrial lines.
KRAS-driven MAPK/MTOR crosstalk may increase mTOR dependence; enriched in sensitive pancreas, lung, ovary, and colorectal lines.
BRAF-mutant tumors often rely on mTOR for survival; observed in sensitive melanoma and colorectal lines.
EGFR activation engages PI3K/AKT/mTOR; EGFR-mutant lung and esophageal lines are sensitive.
MTOR mutation may alter complex activity or drug binding; observed in a highly sensitive colorectal line.
NF1 loss activates RAS/MAPK and may bypass mTOR dependence; enriched in least-affected lines.
STK11/LKB1 loss alters AMPK-mTOR signaling and may reduce sensitivity; seen in least-affected lines.
ATM mutation may reflect alternative DNA-damage survival signaling; enriched in least-affected lines.
CDKN2A loss may uncouple proliferation from mTORC1; seen in least-affected melanoma and soft-tissue lines.
FBXW7 mutation may stabilize oncoproteins and reduce mTOR dependence; enriched in least-affected lines.
TP53 mutation is common in both groups but may contribute to resistance; weak evidence.
